description: Dark green with one bright eye of light at its centre. Mireglare's stare, still lit, still looking.
lore: The test for a real one is barely a test. Shut your fist on it in a dark room and there is still a green line between your fingers. Every other hard piece is a habit or an appetite pressed down until it is very nearly mineral, and mineral does not do anything. This one is lit. Lit is the wrong word for a stone and the trade uses it anyway, having no better.

What it does in a fight follows from what it is. It does not find anything for you. It marks one thing, and after that the thing cannot get out of your sight by stepping out of it — not behind a bank, not into the reeds. The attention does not come off. Fen hunters say the unpleasant part is how quickly you stop bothering to look.

The fen keeps a long vocabulary for what [[monsters/swamp_cat_2|the stare]] is supposed to do to a person, and none of it is true; the animal is only working through faces. The stone settles a harder question, and settles it badly: break the shape, pick the piece out of the grass, and the checking is still going. It went all the way down and it did not finish. [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] keeps hers on the desk, facing the room. She will not shut a thing that is still looking into a drawer, and she has written in her own margin that she cannot say whether that is courtesy or superstition.
gm_notes: The creature record explains the stare away as checking; the stone is the evidence that the checking outlasts the shape, which no encounter can show. Bettany's desk beat is hers and new — the chronicler who will not file a thing she cannot name. Whatever it is looking for is never stated.
